interest: Wartime and occupation marriage cases, and a Ryukyus marriage ban.
overview: Decimal file 894.4054 covers diplomatic, administrative, and legal matters relating to Japanese marriage and divorce between August 1945 and September 1948. The collection comprises personal petitions, legal inquiries from American citizens and attorneys, State Department legal advisories, and military government despatches concerning cross-national domestic relations during the end of World War II and the Allied occupation. Major topics include the petition for divorce, child custody, and Hungarian repatriation submitted by Margherita Nogami, the Hungarian wife of Japanese cultural expert Soichi Nogami interned at Bedford Springs; inquiries concerning the legal validity of divorces granted under Japanese military occupation in the Philippines and marriages contracted in Shanghai and Japan; and official correspondence and military government proclamations from the Ryukyus Command regarding the promulgation and subsequent repeal of Special Proclamation No. 28, which had criminalized marriage between Ryukyuans and members of the Occupation forces.

subfiles.about: English translation of a petition by Margherita Nogami requesting permission to divorce her Japanese husband, retain custody of their child, resume Hungarian citizenship, and join her mother in Germany.
subfiles.from: Margherita Nogami (translated by Central Translating Division, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Margherita Nogami petitions American authorities for a divorce from her husband Professor Soichi Nogami, custody of their infant daughter, resumption of Hungarian citizenship, and repatriation to Regensburg, Germany. She chronicles her marriage in Rome in 1943, her husband's neglect and physical abuse in Venice, their evacuation through Germany with the Japanese diplomatic colony, and his violent attacks against her and her mother during the flight. After separating at Zwiesel in April 1945, the family was interned by U.S. forces, transferred to Le Havre, and moved to Bedford Springs, Pennsylvania, where she continues to seek legal separation.
subfiles.title: Translation of Petition by Margherita Nogami for Divorce, Child Custody, and Resumption of Hungarian Citizenship

subfiles.about: Original Italian handwritten/typed petition and autobiographical curriculum vitae submitted by Margherita Nogami detailing domestic abuse by her husband and requesting divorce, custody, and repatriation.
subfiles.summary: Margherita Nogami submits a formal petition in Italian to the American authorities asking to divorce Soichi Nogami on American soil, retain custody of their daughter Mitsuko Maria Beatrice, renounce Japanese nationality for Hungarian nationality, and return to her mother in Regensburg. She provides a comprehensive autobiographical statement describing her wedding in Rome, her husband's drunkenness and abandonment in Venice, and repeated physical assaults during their evacuation across Bavaria. She recounts being assisted by UNRRA representatives in Fürth im Wald and requests protection from her husband while interned at Bedford Springs.
subfiles.title: Italian Petition and Statement of Margherita Nogami Requesting Divorce and Repatriation

subfiles.about: Telegraphic inquiry from Thomas Hackworth regarding whether an American citizen's marriage in Japan under Japanese law is valid and recognized internationally.
